summary: Elmer Henry Cutts was an indologist and historian who earned his B.A. from the University of Washington and Ph.D. from Harvard. He held posts at the University of Washington, Tufts, and Northeastern, and founded Andhra University in 1958.
Elof Olesen was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Copenhagen from 1895 to 1903, earning an M.A. under the instruction of Michael Viggo Fausbøll.

Elpidius Pax was a scholar of linguistics and religious studies. He studied at Breslau under Wilhelm Havers and Otto Strauss, Munich, and the Pontifical Institute, later serving as professor at Studium Biblicum Franciscanum and Dormition Abbey.
Else Lüders was a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Heinrich Lüders and received an honorary Dr. phil. from the University of Rostock around 1919.

Else Pauly was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Copenhagen under Louis Trolle Hjelmslev and Poul Tuxen. She later served there as a part-time lecturer in Pāli from 1973 to 1979.

Else Wohlgemuth was a scholar of Indology and Sinology. She studied at Humboldt University of Berlin, the University of Marburg, and the University of Leipzig, where she earned her Ph.D. under Ernst Windisch in 1916.

Emanuel Sarkisyanz worked in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tehran and completed his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago, later serving as Head at Heidelberg University starting in 1967.

Emanuela Garatti is a Tibetologist who earned her doctorate from the École Pratique des Hautes Études. She held an affiliation at the University of Munich in 2018 and served as an ATER at EPHE in 2022.

Embar Krishnamacharya was an Indologist. He served as an editor for the Gaekwad's Oriental Series, a Pandit at the Oriental Manuscripts Library, and held posts at Sanskrit Pathashala, Vadtal, and Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya, Vadodara.

Emi Matsushita is a historian and archaeologist. She studied at Nanzan University, the University of East Anglia, and Ohio State University under John C. Huntington, later working as a lecturer in Shizuoka and graduate assistant at Ohio State.

Emil Abegg was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Zurich and Leipzig under Kaegi, Windisch, Sievers, and Conrady, later serving as PD and then professor at the University of Zurich from 1928 to 1955.

Emil Ernst Strohal was an Indologist who studied at the universities of Graz, Vienna, Leipzig, and Göttingen under Johann Kirste, Georg Bühler, and Franz Kielhorn, earning his Ph.D. under Ernst Windisch in 1900.

Emil Franke was an Indologist who studied at Charles University under Josef Zubatý, as well as the universities of Vienna and Berlin. He worked at the National Library of the Czech Republic from circa 1905 to 1918.

Emil Rödiger was a scholar of linguistics and religious studies who studied at Halle-Wittenberg. He held professorships at Halle-Wittenberg and Humboldt University of Berlin, and served as Geschäftsführer of the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft.
Emil Schlagintweit was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied law at Humboldt University of Berlin, was tutored by Franz Joseph Lauth, and served as a Bavarian Regierungsrat.

Emil Schmidt was an Indologist and historian who earned an M.D. from Humboldt University of Berlin and studied at Jena, Leipzig, and Bonn. He subsequently served as PD and professor of ethnology at the University of Leipzig.

Emil Sieg was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Kielhorn, Kuhn, Weber, Geldner, and Schmidt, earning a Ph.D. at Berlin, and held a chair at Göttingen from 1920.

Emile Joseph Dillon was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at several institutions, earning degrees from Saint Petersburg, KU Leuven, and Kharkiv, where he became a professor in 1884.

Emilio Bartoli was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Michele Kerbaker. He taught Latin and Greek at Liceo Vittorio Emanuele II and was a Docente of comparative grammar and Sanskrit at the University of Naples Federico II.

Emilio Lovarini was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Padua. He served as a Docent of Italian Literature at the University of Bologna and taught at Liceo Ginnasio Luigi Galvani and Liceo Artistico di Bologna.
